'''Ajay Mitchell''' (born 25 June 2002) is a Belgian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara Gauchos]]. Mitchell was selected with the 38th overall pick in the second round of the [[2024 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]], but was immediately traded to the Thunder on draft night. During his rookie season with the Thunder, Mitchell won his first [[NBA championship]] in the [[2025 NBA Finals|2025 NBA finals]]. He has also played for the [[Belgium men's national basketball team|Belgium national team]].

==Early life and career==
Mitchell grew up in [[Ans, Belgium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dhnet.be/sports/basket/2021/06/22/ajay-mitchell-quitte-limburg-pour-cal-state-santa-barbara-46UFJCXSXZEINPBUJUC2EFQNF4/|title=Ajay Mitchell quitte Limburg pour Cal State Santa Barbara|work=[[La Dernière Heure]]|date=22 June 2021|access-date=7 March 2023|language=French}}</ref> At age 17, he moved to France for a period of a few months, where he played thirteen games in the under-18 team of [[Nanterre 92]] along with [[Victor Wembanyama]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Van frêle tiener en ploegmaat van de jonge Wembanyama naar het basketbalwalhalla: wie is NBA-Belg Ajay Mitchell? {{!}} sporza |url=https://sporza.be/nl/2024/06/25/van-frele-tiener-en-ploegmaat-van-de-jonge-wembanyama-naar-het-basketbalwalhalla-wie-is-nba-belg-ajay-mitchell~1719310029350/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240628130902/https://sporza.be/nl/2024/06/25/van-frele-tiener-en-ploegmaat-van-de-jonge-wembanyama-naar-het-basketbalwalhalla-wie-is-nba-belg-ajay-mitchell~1719310029350/ |archive-date=28 June 2024 |access-date=15 December 2024 |work=sporza.be |language=nl-BE}}</ref> He began playing for [[Limburg United]]'s youth team in 2019 and made two appearances with the senior team in the [[Pro Basketball League]] during the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lavenir.net/sports/2021/01/31/des-liegeois-sans-ressort-ecrases-a-limburg-QXD37OCXEFDOZFTXNKRJL3AYV4/|title=Des Liégeois sans ressort écrasés à Limburg|work=[[L'Avenir (Belgian newspaper)|L'Avenir]]|date=31 January 2021|access-date=7 March 2023|language=French}}</ref> 

Mitchell played solely with the senior team during the 2020–21 season while maintaining his amateur status. After the season, he committed to playing college basketball for [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]].<ref name="commit">{{cite web|url=https://newspress.com/belgian-basketball-star-commits-to-play-for-ucsb/|title=Belgian basketball star commits to play for UCSB|work=[[Santa Barbara News-Press]]|date=7 September 2020|access-date=7 March 2023|archive-date=8 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308003158/https://newspress.com/belgian-basketball-star-commits-to-play-for-ucsb/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Mitchell played in 27 games during his freshman season and was named the [[Big West Conference]] Freshman of the Year and second team All-Big West after averaging 11.6 points, 3.7 assists, and 2.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.noozhawk.com/mark-patton-ajay-mitchell-can-now-talk-the-talk-with-ucsb-basketball/|title=Mark Patton: Ajay Mitchell Can Now Talk the Talk with UCSB Basketball|website=[[Noozhawk]]|date=4 December 2022|access-date=7 March 2023}}</ref> He averaged 16.3 points, 5.1 assists, and 2.7 rebounds per game and was named the [[Big West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big West Player of the Year]] during his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.noozhawk.com/ucsb-sophomore-ajay-mitchell-honored-as-big-west-player-of-year/|title=UCSB Sophomore Ajay Mitchell Honored as Big West Basketball Player of Year|website=[[Noozhawk]]|date=6 March 2023|access-date=7 March 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On 27 June 2024, Mitchell was selected with the 38th overall pick by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2024 NBA Draft]]; however, immediately on draft night, he was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for the 40th overall pick in the 2024 draft and cash.<ref>{{cite web|first=Enzo|last=Flojo|title=Thunder 2024 NBA Draft grades for every pick|url=https://clutchpoints.com/thunder-2024-nba-draft-grades-every-pick|website=ClutchPoints|date=28 June 2024|access-date=28 June 2024}}</ref> On 6 July, Mitchell signed a two-way contract with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Nikola Topić and Dillon Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/topic-jones-mitchell-240706|website=NBA.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=7 July 2024}}</ref> During his first regular season, he would post a career-high 26 points against the [[Indiana Pacers]] on October 23rd. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Ajay Mitchell Career High |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/ajay-mitchell-career-high |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref>

On 10 January 2025, Mitchell was ruled out for 10-to-12 weeks after undergoing surgery to repair a [[metatarsophalangeal joint sprain|turf toe sprain]] in the great toe on his right foot.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OKC Thunder Rookie Ajay Mitchell Undergoes Surgery, injury Timeline|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/okc-thunder-rookie-ajay-mitchell-undergoes-surgery-injury-timeline|access-date=12 January 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref> On 6 February, the Thunder officially converted Mitchell to a standard contract, signing him to a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Ajay Mitchell to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-mitchell-250206|website=NBA.com|date=6 February 2025|access-date=20 March 2025}}</ref> On 22 June, the Thunder won the [[List of NBA champions|NBA title]], making Mitchell the second Belgian NBA champion, after [[D. J. Mbenga]]. On 30 June, Mitchell re-signed with the Thunder on a three-year, $9 million contract.<ref>{{cite web | last=Stiles | first=Rylan | title=OKC Thunder: Grading Ajay Mitchell Contract Extension | website=Oklahoma City Thunder On SI | date=2025-06-30 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/onsi/news/okc-thunder-grading-ajay-mitchell-contract-extension | access-date=2025-12-05}}</ref> He delivered a playoff-high 28 points on May 11 against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[NBA Semifinals|Western Conference Semi-Finals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ajay Mitchell lights it up in L.A. helping Thunder go up 3-0 {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/ajay-mitchell-mix-long |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Mitchell played for the [[Belgium national under-19 basketball team|Belgium under-18 team]], before making his debut with the [[Belgium men's national basketball team|senior team]] at age 18 in 2021.<ref name=":0" />

==Personal life==
Born to Belgian Fabienne Wagemans and [[Barry Mitchell (basketball)|Barry Mitchell]] who played college basketball at Norfolk State and professionally in the [[Continental Basketball Association]] and [[World Basketball League]] before leaving a legacy in Belgian basketball.<ref name=commit/> He is a [[Christian]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Emily |date=13 May 2026 |title= Oklahoma City Thunder Guard Ajay Mitchell Says Understanding the Gospel ‘Changed My Perspective on Life’  |url=https://relevantmagazine.com/culture/sports/oklahoma-city-thunder-guard-ajay-mitchell-says-understanding-the-gospel-changed-my-perspective-on-life/ |website=Relevant Magazine |location= |publisher= |access-date=}}</ref>
